licensure.disciplinary_grounds.rationale: These nine buckets cleanly partition the distribution by separating the two dominant fraud clusters (obtaining credentials vs. practice/billing fraud), criminal history, physical/mental/substance impairment, skill-based failures, broad ethics/conduct violations, statutory or board-order non-compliance, out-of-state or other-authority adverse actions, and the recurring ground of facilitating unlicensed practice—leaving no major cluster without a natural home.

profession_specific.license_type_structu.rationale: The data clusters around the regulatory modality (licensed vs. certified), the professional title (dietitian, nutritionist, or combined dietitian-nutritionist), and several structurally distinct sub-types (provisional/temporary permits, dietetic technicians, and edge cases like compact privilege or graduate permits), which together cover the full distribution without over-splitting.

profession_specific.alternative_credenti.rationale: The items naturally cluster into five groups: the Certified Nutrition Specialist (CNS/BCNS) credential, the American Clinical Board of Nutrition Diplomate (DACBN/ACBN), the American Board of Nutrition (ABN) diplomate/membership, professional society memberships (AIN, ASCN), and the advanced academic degree pathway unique to California.

profession_specific.protected_titles.rationale: The protected titles cluster by credential type (licensed, registered, certified, or bare), by professional role (dietitian vs. nutritionist vs. combined vs. therapy/counselor/specialist vs. dietetic technician), and by form (full word title vs. abbreviation/initialism), giving every item a natural home without over-relying on a catch-all.
